scope: unmerged downstream FreeCAD development C++ importer SOLID OCS patch
build: Headless macOS ARM64 AppleClang 21, CMake 4.4.5, Qt 6.12, OCCT 7.9.3, Python 3.12; temporary yaml-cpp 0.8.0 and Xerces-C 3.2.5; exact source archive with two C++ source files modified by the candidate patch.
change: Use absolute normal components in the arbitrary-axis threshold, normalize its X axis, and apply the resulting OCS transform to SOLID corners before creating geometry.

validation.baseline: Original native Import.readDXF into isolated fresh documents: negative-axis and oblique SOLIDs retain raw OCS vertices; default SOLID and following LINE correct. Proposed upstream generated-source test fails both nondefault cases.
validation.patched: The proposed FreeCAD import test passes default, negative, oblique, and non-unit extrusion normals. Three separate generated direct controls match independent expected WCS vertices and areas and retain the following LINE. Four generated controls match expected outer App::Link geometry through two 90-degree inserts for negative and oblique normals in millimetres and inches.
validation.oracle: Expected WCS points computed independently with ezdxf 1.4.5 OCS and analytic insert transforms; expected SOLID area is 12 square drawing units, converted to square millimetres.
validation.packaging: Patch applies cleanly to exact source files; generated test compiles and runs against both baseline and patched importer. Scratch DXFs are not committed.

limits: Patch is unmerged and has not been run in FreeCAD GUI, on Linux/Windows, against producer-authored inputs, thickness or arbitrary transforms.
Shared OCS basis affects additional consumer paths that need their own native regression.
The direct test uses Import.readDXF into a new document and is not the complete GUI open/insert workflow.
No phase or format support claim is promoted.
